messages:
alex: EDR flagged a persistent daemon on my macbook: 'updatersvc' spawning a net client to 45.77.12.9:443. EDR quarantined the binary and auto-isolated the host. tagging eng-security for triage

edr-bot: [automated] AlertID: A-2026-0927, Path: /Users/alex/.local/bin/updatersvc, SHA256: d4f7a9b3... , PID: 5312, Parent: launchd, Outbound IPs: 45.77.12.9:443. Actions taken: quarantine file, isolate network.

opsbot: Created incident INC-2026-457 and assigned to chris-sec + alex — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-457

mary-soc: Confirming: is the host fully isolated from corporate network (no VPN, no LAN)? If not, isolate immediately. Collect EDR full bundle + memory capture.

alex: Host shows as isolated in EDR console. Running full-diagnostic + memory capture now, ETA ~10m.

chris-sec: Good. Short checklist: 1) collect EDR logs + memory 2) list recent SSH sessions and active kube/API tokens 3) check KMS access events for this principal 4) snapshot /Users/alex for artifacts. Avoid reboot until memory capture finishes.

nina: quick triage from remote: lsof indicates established connection from updatersvc -> 45.77.12.9 and a temp file at /tmp/.sessXXXX. No obvious scp uploads in the EDR network history but need packet capture to be sure.

sam: If there's any chance infra creds lived on that host, rotate them now. Recommend revoking short-lived tokens, block CI PATs if present, and schedule reimage. Who is the device owner?

alex: I am the owner. I don't recall storing infra PATs locally, but I do have a personal gh CLI and docker creds for dev. Running `env | grep -i token` — no obvious PATs shown. Will still rotate tokens as precaution.

chris-sec: Also check cloud audit logs for any KMS Decrypt/Encrypt or IAM token creation events around the timeframe (t0 -5m to t0 +15m). If KMS was used, rotate keys or rotate access policies and revoke sessions that used the key.

mary-soc: Add SIEM events for the user and mark as high priority. Legal/Privacy on standby in case of data exposure. Post-incident actions: tighten RBAC for local installer permissions, add audit hooks for new daemon launches, and ensure KMS key usage logs are forwarded to the SIEM.

alex: attaching snippet of ps/netstat I ran:
```
$ ps aux | grep updatersvc
alex       5312  0.3  1.2  431234  9824 ?  S    09:21   0:02 /Users/alex/.local/bin/updatersvc --conn 45.77.12.9:443
$ lsof -iTCP -nP | grep 45.77.12.9
updatersvc 5312 alex   12u  IPv4 0x... TCP 192.0.2.12:54321->45.77.12.9:443 (ESTABLISHED)
```

chris-sec: Nice. Add that exact SHA to the incident ticket and mark the hash as blocked in EDR/MDM. We'll also push an MDM policy to block autorun locations under ~/.local/bin and quarantine any matching hashes fleet-wide.

nina: :eyes: Suggest we also add a streaming alert for unknown outbound IPs during business hours and a rule to escalate to SOC automatically.

sam: Agree. Ops: revoke laptop certs / SSH keys tied to this machine and force MFA reauth for cloud consoles that alex used in last 24h.

mary-soc: For the postmortem: timeline, root cause (how binary landed), whether creds accessed, and remediation (RBAC changes, KMS policy updates, audit log retention changes). Also include who approved the reimage.

alex: I'll upload the EDR bundle + memory capture to the ticket and hold the machine for forensic imaging. I'll also rotate my GH and Docker creds and list anything I ran in past 24h.

opsbot: INC-2026-457 updated: "evidence attached by alex". SLA: 4h initial triage.

chris-sec: Plan after triage: 1) reimage device 2) block the hash + outbound IP 3) rotate any exposed secrets 4) add RBAC rule to prevent local installs without MDM approval 5) review KMS key policies to require principal and source context.

mary-soc: Meeting in 30 to confirm actions. Please be ready to share the EDR bundle link and the SHA. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

alex: On it, will be online for the call.
